record.title_md: Universal point sets for planar graphs
record.subject: Drawings

dossier_meta.catalog_title: Universal point sets for planar graphs
dossier_meta.subject: Graph Theory » Topological Graph Theory » Drawings
dossier_meta.statement_text: We say that a set $ P \subseteq {\mathbb R}^2 $ is $ n $ - universal if every $ n $ vertex planar graph can be drawn in the plane so that each vertex maps to a distinct point in $ P $ , and all edges are (non-intersecting) straight line segments. Question Does there exist an $ n $ -universal set of size $ O(n) $ ?
dossier_meta.context_text: More generally, if we let $ f(n) $ denote the size of the smallest $ n $ -universal set, we are interested in the behaviour of $ f $ . The best known upper bound is $ f(n) = O(n^2) $ . Indeed, every $ n $ -vertex planar graph can be drawn as required in the $ n \times n $ grid [dFPP], [S]. On the flip side, it is known that $ f(n) \ge 1.098n $ for sufficiently large $ n $ [CH].
dossier_meta.references_text:
- [CH] M. Chrobak and H.Karloff. A lower bound on the size of universal sets for planar graphs. SIGACT News, 20:83-86, 1989.
- [dFPP] H. de Fraysseix, J. Pach, and R. Pollack. How to draw a planar graph on a grid. Combinatorica, 10(1):41-51, 1990. MathSciNet
- [S] W. Schnyder. Embedding planar graphs on the grid. In Proc. 1st ACM-SIAM Sympos. Discrete Algorithms, pages 138-148, 1990.
